title: Periodic Compliance Evidence Digest and Signed Delivery Channels
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: deliver a tenant-scoped, residency-aware periodic "evidence digest" that bundles exportable artifacts (PDF/CSV) with a cryptographically signed delivery manifest and configurable delivery channels. The digest must include retention metadata (applied retention policy, deletion schedule, residency region), proof of provenance (checksums, signature), and a delivery audit record visible in the Console dashboard. It should support scheduled deliveries (daily/weekly/monthly), on-demand generation, and multiple transports (S3 with presigned manifests, secure FTP, email with S/MIME, and customer-managed S3 endpoints for Private customers).
acceptance_criteria: Generate tenant-scoped PDF and CSV artifacts that include per-record residency and retention annotations
Create a signed manifest (JSON) with checksums, KMS key id, and delivery timestamp; manifest must be verifiable using customer or Redwood public key
Support scheduling UI in Console for daily/weekly/monthly deliveries with timezone and blackout windows
Delivery transports: Redwood-hosted S3 bucket (with presigned URL), direct S3 push to tenant endpoint, SFTP upload, and email attachment with size fallback to presigned link
Console dashboard shows history of digests (status: queued/sent/failed), per-digest telemetry (size, record-count, residency distribution), and a link to the signed manifest
Retention metadata in digest is derived from active tenant retention policy; digest flags records that are pending deletion and earliest deletion timestamp
Retry policy for transient failures with exponential backoff and alerting to tenant owner on prolonged failures (>72h)
Security review completed and KMS/HSM key usage documented before enabling for Private deployments
implementation_notes: Back-end will reuse existing export worker with new 'digest' assembler that attaches retention/residency metadata and creates PDF summary pages
Manifest signing: use AWS KMS sign for hosted customers; support optional customer-supplied public key for verification in Private/VPC installs
Compression: use TAR+GZIP for multi-file digests and include manifest at top-level; support single-file CSV or single-PDF digests for small tenants
PII handling: redact fields marked sensitive by tenant schema or apply field-level hashing; provide opt-out toggle per tenant
Delivery guarantees: at-least-once for S3/SFTP, with deduplication by manifest-id on recipient side; ensure idempotency for retries
Observability: emit export.metrics.{tenant,region,status,size,record_count} and link trace id to Console UI for troubleshooting
Scale: shard digest generation by tenant-residency region to respect data residency; maintain per-region worker pools
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Kumar: Created ticket and sketched initial UX flows. Punted detailed retention edge cases to implementation notes.
2026-03-11 - Ravi Patel: Scoped transports and confirmed S3 + SFTP + email cover 95% of target customers. Asked Eng to provide cost estimate for daily digests.
2026-03-11 - Eng feedback (ENG-9134): Need KMS signing prototype before enabling automated customer verification; suggested using a manifest envelope format that supports multiple signatures.
2026-03-11 - Design review: dashboard needs a compact timeline view and ability to filter by residency region. Mockups uploaded to Drive link.
risk: Key management and cross-region residency routing are the highest risk areas. Incorrectly including records outside tenant residency would be a regulatory failure. Delivery failures could cause legal SLA breaches.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (beta): enable for hosted tenants only, daily/weekly options, S3 presigned link and Console dashboard visibility
Phase 2: add SFTP push and email delivery; introduce signed manifest verification using Redwood public key
Phase 3: Private/VPC: support customer-supplied public key and direct S3 push to tenant-managed buckets; harden KMS/HSM audit trails
Canary: start with 10 low-risk tenants in US region for 2 weeks, evaluate failures and retention mapping accuracy before broader rollout
